config_changes.change: Quorum worker model changed from claude-sonnet-5-5 to claude-opus-5-5 (quorum.py provider.model("opus"))

new sandbox tool jlabel: labels rows with Jev (TypeSafe System One choice/noul questions) through a host-side proxy (sq/jlabel_proxy.py); per-trial label-only token, 20000-item budget, requests and responses kept in jlabel.jsonl per trial; one generic line added to the worker prompt; each row is labelled in 3 Jev passes and the probabilities are averaged (Jev is not deterministic: 4 of 111 identical rows flipped between two single-pass jobs, 1 of 111 with 3-pass averaging); a per-trial cache keeps repeated rows consistent; no cache is shared between trials; version 2 after a first version made trials stall: labelling is time-bounded (150 s per call, progress saved to a cache file, rerun the same command to continue) because a tool call over about 4 minutes ends the whole worker session; the proxy uses 64 workers and averages 3 passes only on rows where the first pass is below 0.9 confidence; item budget 60000 per trial; version 3 after TypeSafe API credits ran out mid-run (HTTP 402): the proxy no longer retries billing failures, caps Jev calls in flight at 48 across trials, bounds every request to 90 s, refuses requests immediately while Jev is down; the runner holds (label_down) until a probe call succeeds and discards and reruns any trial that overlapped a billing failure; Jev is reached through OpenRouter (JLABEL_BACKEND=openrouter) because the direct TypeSafe credits ran out; not through jev-router, which routes chat requests to other models; labels are shared within a trial by row and category names, not wording, because parallel worker sessions were each labelling the same ~6,700 rows (about 3x redundant work); the worker prompt asks it to label only the rows it needs
config_changes.reason: per-row text classification was done by the worker reading each row (no classifier tool in the kit), which varied run to run

config_changes: v6: added sq/overlay (editable prompt overlay files) and sq/audit.py (completeness audit: tool-less Opus checks the answer against the question wording; an incomplete answer triggers one repeat with the missing items named and a widened answer format); the audit design was motivated by an answer-shape omission noticed while reviewing a solo-v5 trial against the earlier baseline, so scores were visible when this step was designed

v6 loop: three improvement sets, each written by an Opus editor from trial traces only (questions, answers, attempt status, tool errors, timings); the editor receives no score, reference answer or validator; no edit is kept or reverted by score; each set is followed by one 54-query pass (run ids 0-2)

v6 run 3 rerun: the first run 3 hit Anthropic credit exhaustion in the workers (31 of 54 trials produced empty answers; archived at runtime/runs/submission-r2-credit-outage-superseded). Before the rerun, one worker overlay line written by improvement set 2 ("you cannot create files here") was corrected by hand because it contradicted the query/label tools, which save under /home/ide/dab-work; the runner now discards and reruns any trial whose workers report a credit error. The whole of run 3 was rerun, not only the affected trials.

v6 stability experiment (diagnostic, not a leaderboard run): (a) generic single-attempt mode: no repeats, no completeness audit, no adjudication, no answer selection (infrastructure retry of an attempt that never ran is kept); (b) intake now declares typed value columns (name, string|integer|number|boolean, unit) for every value the question requests and folds them into the format text; (c) three messy-data / complete-answer lines added to the worker overlay, adopted from reading a public leaderboard submission (PR 121) for ideas, not text; (d) the 11 tasks that failed at least once in v6 runs 1-3 were rerun three times each (run ids 3-5), a subset chosen by earlier scores: these reruns measure stability only and must not be reported as a pass rate.

v7 specialist-tools experiment (diagnostic, not a leaderboard run): the worker's single long prompt is split into stages, each backed by a tool that answers in its own context: `sage` (question-aware locator over the code-measured Sage profile: relevant tables/columns/joins, definitions recorded in the data, ambiguous wording; one tool-less Opus call, reads no rows), `joincheck` (code only: measured match rate of two identifier columns as stored and after simple normalisations), `jlabel` (unchanged), `verify` (independent Opus review of the candidate answer, the question and the declared answer shape against the worker's account of how it was computed: missing requested values, shape, method consistency; sees no data and no gold). Calls are capped per task (sage 4, verify 3, USD 1.5) and logged in jlabel.jsonl with their cost. Gate `tools` is on; single-attempt mode is unchanged (no repeats, no selection, no score-based decisions). The tool/stage text contains no dataset, table or query names. The same 11 failed-at-least-once tasks were rerun three times (run ids 6-8): a subset chosen by earlier scores, so these runs measure stability against the earlier runs on the same tasks and must not be reported as a pass rate.

v8 harness layers (diagnostic, same status as v7): (1) stage gate: the database query tools (dbq, dbsnap, dpython) refuse to run until `sage` has been called once (or was unreachable), so the locate stage cannot be skipped; verify stays optional but is logged. (2) requirement contract: one tool-less Opus call on the question wording and declared answer shape only (no data) lists every value to return (ids A1, A2..), the stated filters, grain, aggregation, ordering and terms left undefined; it is added to the worker prompt, the worker lists each id with its value in its claim evidence, and `verify` checks the candidate against it. (3) answer lint: deterministic code (sq/shapelint.py) flags markdown, labels, prose, decimals and thousands separators against the declared shape and too few items against the contract; `verify` prints it before the review. (4) per-trial signals (result.json `signals`): tool calls, joincheck use, verify verdicts, lint, contract coverage; label-free, for reporting only, never used for selection. The same 11 failed-at-least-once tasks were rerun three times (run ids 9-11): a subset chosen by earlier scores, so this measures stability against the earlier runs on the same tasks and must not be reported as a pass rate.

v9 noise-aware tools (diagnostic, same status as v7/v8): (1) `joincheck` reports key and ROW match shares on both sides, fan-out of the join, keys a clean-up would merge, and unmatched keys with their closest partner. (2) new `bounds` tool: the answer with uncertain rows (unmatched join rows, low-confidence labels) all out, all in and probability-weighted. (3) `jlabel` prints per-label count ranges (sure .. possible, expected), writes p_<label> columns, and from 60 rows has an independent Opus judge (specialist `judge`, 4 calls per task, sees only the labelling question, the allowed labels and a random sample of 30 rows) re-label the sample and reports agreement. Tool behaviour is tested on synthetic noise (scripts/dab-tools-selftest.py), not on benchmark data. The same 11 failed-at-least-once tasks were rerun three times (run ids 12-14): a subset chosen by earlier scores, so this measures stability against earlier runs on the same tasks and must not be reported as a pass rate.

v10 (diagnostic, same status as v7-v9): the v7 specialist-tool harness (sage, joincheck, jlabel, verify; no stage gate, no requirement contract) plus the noise-aware tool versions from v9: joincheck row/fan-out/unmatched-key report, `bounds`, and jlabel count ranges with a sampled independent judge. Gates `contract` and `stage_gate` are off (they exist as separate switches since v8; answer lint and per-trial signals stay on, as code-only and logging). Same 11 failed-at-least-once tasks rerun three times (run ids 15-17): a subset chosen by earlier scores, so this measures stability against the earlier runs on the same tasks and must not be reported as a pass rate.

v11 (diagnostic; built from the failure audit in docs/dab-submission/v6-v10-failure-audit.md, which used observer pass/fail labels on these same 11 tasks, so v11 is outcome-informed and these reruns are not held-out): (1) interpretation brief: before the worker starts, three independent tool-less Opus calls on the question wording and declared answer shape only (no data) write a brief (every value to return, the filters the question states, grain/aggregation/ordering, and the reading chosen for each ambiguous term by fixed precedence rules: the task's own definitions first, then the most literal reading, the whole named set not narrowed, format examples and length limits never decide a reading, values returned as stored, ties never removed by changing filters, data-dependent readings left to the data); a fourth call merges them; the worker must follow it or write a DEVIATION line with the query that shows it. (2) `verify` is adversarial and binding: it names the strongest alternative reading, filters nobody asked for, values altered from their stored form, missing values and shape problems, and the worker must apply each fix or answer it with a query result. (3) answer lint (code) also flags ellipses and values shortened relative to the stored form shown in the worker's account. (4) `jlabel` sends the rows it is unsure about (confidence < 0.9, or 0.2 < p_yes < 0.8, up to 120) to an independent judge and writes label_final / yes_final with label_source. (5) `joincheck` no longer exits silently on error. Stage gate off, as in v10. The same 11 failed-at-least-once tasks rerun three times (run ids 18-20): a subset chosen by earlier scores, so this measures stability against earlier runs on the same tasks and must not be reported as a pass rate.

v11 full run (run ids 21-25, 54 tasks x 5 runs): the v11 harness of the entry above on every task. The v11 design was informed by a failure audit that used observer pass/fail labels on 11 of the 54 tasks (DEPS_DEV_V1/query1, GITHUB_REPOS/query1, GITHUB_REPOS/query2, PANCANCER_ATLAS/query1, PATENTS/query1, agnews/query2, agnews/query3, crmarenapro/query12, crmarenapro/query2, crmarenapro/query3, stockmarket/query5); the other 43 were not audited. The harness is therefore outcome-informed, not untuned in the sense of never using benchmark outcomes; results are reported both overall and separately for the 43 never-audited tasks.

v11 full run stopped by the operator before completion: run id 21 completed all 54 tasks; run id 22 stopped with 24 of 54 tasks finished and run ids 23-25 not started (0 results in 23). The unfinished trials were killed and their Quorum runs and sandboxes stopped. All finished v11 results are kept in runtime/runs/submission-r21 and submission-r22 and are not part of any final number; they are the baseline for the v12 changes below.

v12 (outcome-informed: built from a failure audit of the v11 first full pass (run id 21, 8 failed tasks) plus the earlier audits, using observer pass/fail labels, so it is NOT untuned in the sense of never using benchmark outcomes): (1) the interpretation brief now treats every object of the main verb as a separate value to return, lets a task-given definition outrank the wording rules (never explained away), resolves scope questions by the rules instead of deferring to the data, lists at most four material readings and states values-as-stored with a separator-collision rule; (2) intake acceptance checks may no longer count separator-delimited fields; (3) `verify` takes its text from files (the shell altered `$20` and backticks inside double quotes), flags readings with no computed result, filters nobody asked for (only ever recommending their removal), altered values, missing values and low coverage, may not put candidate values in its suggested shape, and its fixes on altered values, unrequested filters, missing values and uncomputed readings cannot be overridden by a DEVIATION line; (4) the worker records a READING-CHECK line for every reading the brief lists and the surviving share after each join or filter; (5) `jlabel` calibrates with a stratified judge sample drawn from every label and reports counts corrected for the measured confusion with an approximate 95% interval, and says so when the judge is unreachable. Full 54 task x 5 run measurement: run ids 26-30.
